findings.title: Protect unsubscribe mutations against CSRF
findings.body: The new GET endpoints change the logged-in user's notification settings without a signed unsubscribe token. Rails does not require CSRF tokens for GET requests, and this action also bypasses the XHR check. A third-party page can therefore request a predictable URL such as /t/123/unsubscribe.json in an authenticated browser and silently lower or mute that user's notifications. Keep GET read-only and perform the change through a CSRF-protected request, or validate a recipient-specific unsubscribe token.

findings.title: Handle users without an existing TopicUser record
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a logged-in user who has never interacted with this topic. For example, this happens when a public-topic email link is forwarded or opened while logged into a different account. TopicView does not establish that a TopicUser row exists, so dereferencing tu.notification_level raises an exception and returns a server error. Treat a missing row as the default notification level and use the create-or-update path when unsubscribing.

findings.title: Persist unsubscribe as an explicit notification preference
findings.body: Saving only notification_level leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged. For a user whose reason is nil, an unsubscribe that sets the topic to muted can later be undone by TopicUser.update_last_read: that method automatically assigns tracking whenever the reason is nil and the reading-time threshold is met. Thus reading the topic can unmute an explicitly unsubscribed user. Use TopicUser.change, or otherwise record the user_changed reason and notification-change timestamp along with the new level.

findings.title: Unsubscribe when the URL is reached through client-side navigation
findings.body: This route only loads the ordinary topic view; it never invokes the unsubscribe action or changes the notification level. The preference changes only when a full-page request reaches TopicsController#unsubscribe. If the URL is followed through an Ember transition, such as a same-site link while the application is already running, the page displays the unsubscribe confirmation while the user remains subscribed. Ensure the operation is performed for client-side navigation too, rather than relying on the initial HTML request.

findings.title: Mute watched topics for mailing-list recipients
findings.body: The new per-topic link is also included in emails generated by mailing_list_notify. However, for a mailing-list user whose topic is watching or tracking, this branch only lowers the level to regular. Regular does not opt a topic out of mailing-list delivery, so subsequent posts keep producing the same emails despite the unsubscribe confirmation. Mailing-list recipients need the topic muted to stop those emails; account for mailing_list_mode when choosing the new level.
